To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of DPH and T‐DPH probes in isolated rat hepatocyte membranes revealed significant differences in membrane fluidity values compared with membrane fractions and subcellular fractions, probably due to differences in the location of these probes in the membrane bilayer.
the use of TMA‐DPF as a fluorescent probe in isolated rat hepatocyte membranes is more reliable than DPH.
the use of DPH and TMD‐DPH as probes of membrane fluidity in hepatocytes revealed different results.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determination in isolated rat hepatocyte plasma membrane fluidity, which is a fundamental parameter in membrane function.
the study of plasma membrane fluidity in intact hepatocytes and its comparison with membrane fractions and subfractionation.

the determination, by the use of fluorescent probes, of the fluidity of plasma membrane in isolated rat hepatocyte and in membrane fractions and subcellular fractions derived from hepatocyte homogenates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
membrane fluidity of hepatocytes is lower than that of the plasma membrane fractions, and that TMA‐DHP is the probe of choice for measuring the fluidity of whole isolated hepatocyte preparations.
the plasma membrane of isolated hepatocytes is more fluid than that of plasma membrane fractions and that the membrane fluidity of hepatocytes is not homogeneous.
membrane fluidity in hepatocytes can be measured using DPH and/or TMA‐DP H and that the values obtained are comparable in isolated hepatocytes and in subcellular membrane fractions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the membrane fluidity of the hepatocytes is similar to that of the membrane fractions and subcellular fractions derived from homogenization.
the membrane fluidity of the plasma membrane of isolated rat hepatocyte is lower than that of plasma membrane fractions and is similar to that of subfractions derived from homogenized liver.
membrane fluidity is not a static parameter, but a dynamic one which is dependent on the probe used, the cell type, the temperature, and the experimental conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of DPH and TMD‐DPH as probes for measuring the fluidity of the plasma membrane of isolated hepatocytes is a valid approach.
TMA‐DHP is a better probe for the measurement of the membrane fluidity of hepatocytes than DPH.
the membrane fluidity in hepatocytes is higher than that in plasma membrane fractions or subfractions, and that this difference is more pronounced at 37°C than at 25°C.
